KeyValet is a local credential broker for AI agents on macOS: API keys, tokens and OAuth accounts live in a Secure Enclave-protected, root-only vault, and agents get approved, scoped use — proxied calls, derived tokens, or explicit reads — instead of the raw secrets. This is the first tagged release.

## Highlights

- **Secure Enclave-backed vault.** Each session unlock derives the vault key from a CryptoKit Secure Enclave P-256 key (`userPresence` ACL) and mixes it with a root-only device binding secret, so a copied `vault.enc` can't be opened by one approved prompt alone. Each key change creates a fresh `device-binding-<id>.key`. A separate Argon2id recovery passphrase is the independent offline path (`keyvalet recovery-read` / `recover-vault` / `rotate-recovery`). Every session unlock requires Touch ID or the login password, including inside `remember` windows.
- **Approvals bound to the exact request.** Per-use grants bind to the complete operation — method, host, path, query, headers and a body preview for proxied calls; scopes, repositories and permissions for tokens; lifetime for AWS credentials. Grant modes: per-use, per-credential (default), per-session, remember-for-N-hours. Loosening always requires device-owner authentication.
- **Use without disclosure.** `proxy_only` credentials are never returned by `get`; agents receive derived, short-lived material (access tokens, installation tokens, signed JWTs, TOTP codes, STS credentials) or proxied responses. A loopback-only token-gated gateway (`credential_gateway`) is available for agents that need direct HTTP access.
- **Audit.** Every unlock, grant, read, token fetch, proxied call and configuration change is appended to a root-only audit log; secret values are never logged.
- **Credential kinds.** Static secrets (50 bundled service templates plus 4 generic ones), OAuth 2.0, Google service accounts, GitHub Apps, JWT, TOTP, AWS STS.
- **Runtimes.** Claude Code (primary target, exercised every session: MCP server, `UserPromptSubmit`/`PreToolUse` hooks, `/keyvalet:*` commands, plugin). Cursor (plugin bundle with native hooks; medium-high confidence from the documented contract, not run against a live session). Devin CLI (plugin with native hooks; medium confidence, hook payloads covered by unit tests). Grok Build (native hook file; low-medium confidence). Codex (best-effort hook config; low confidence). Other MCP clients work as a plain stdio server. See `docs/runtimes.md` for the per-runtime confidence notes.

## Requirements

- Apple Silicon Mac (prebuilt binaries are arm64 only; Intel Macs fall back to a source build)
- macOS 14 or later (tested on macOS 26.5.1)
- Touch ID or the macOS login password for approvals

## Install

```sh
curl -fsSL https://keyvalet.dev/install.sh | sh
```

On Apple Silicon this downloads the arm64 package attached to this release and verifies it against `SHA256SUMS` before installing. Source build (Intel, or if no release asset is available) requires the Rust toolchain and Xcode Command Line Tools. Manage the vault with `keyvalet help`; uninstall with `curl -fsSL https://keyvalet.dev/install.sh | sh -s -- --uninstall`.

## Known limitations

- **Intel Macs:** no prebuilt binaries; they build from source. Secure Enclave on T2 Macs is untested.
- **macOS versions:** tested on 26.5.1 only; 14 through 25 are within the declared deployment target but not yet exercised — headless/SSH sessions and devices without Touch ID (password fallback) still need release-matrix validation.
- **Release integrity:** the archive is verified against the `SHA256SUMS` file published in the same GitHub release — an integrity check, not a signature. There is no codesigning identity beyond an ad-hoc hardened-runtime signature and no notarization.
- **Threat model:** root or kernel compromise, a compromised build, and physical attacks are out of scope — see `SECURITY.md` for the full boundary.
